extracted.intended_audience: independent nonfiction documentary filmmakers applying to the Sundance Institute Documentary Fund
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility criteria for submitting feature-length nonfiction documentary projects to the Sundance Institute Documentary Fund, including required materials, formats, timing, and the committee’s evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and submission windows
rubrics_metrics.description: The Documentary Fund accepts submissions through periodic open calls; the next call closes on July 14, 2025, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who submit by the posted deadline will be notified in early 2026. It is free to apply on or before the posted deadline; late submissions may require a fee and are not guaranteed to be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: No deadline extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The program does not offer deadline extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions typically take six to eight months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not contact the program for status updates; award notifications are sent by email. Some grants are announced periodically and are not individual notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate project phase for application
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit when you have written or visual material demonstrating creative and storytelling intent; you may submit at any phase from development through post-production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All proposals must convey some vision for a finished film, have secured characters or participants, be able to articulate a story or structure, and explain the project’s driving central question. The Fund cannot consider proposals for story research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing relative to picture lock / premieres
rubrics_metrics.description: Once your film reaches picture lock or premieres, the Fund is unable to provide post-production funding support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to apply at least eight months before planned picture lock or an anticipated premiere. Picture-locked cuts are ineligible for post-production funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of films supported
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports cinematic documentaries embracing a wide range of aesthetic traditions and storytelling approaches by artists who demonstrate a clarity of vision, distinct voice, and meaningful connection to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hybrid and experimental documentaries are eligible. The Fund is not theme-bound and welcomes global aesthetic traditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible film types
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund does not fund fiction films, short films, series, NGO films, advocacy films, educational films, or branded content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purely historical or biographical films are generally not funded unless they show clear contemporary relevance or innovation in form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short film policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Stand-alone short films are not funded through the Documentary Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a separate Documentary Short Fund with changing priorities; check the website for current calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finished project/completion funding ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Film transfers, film prints, and debt reimbursement to complete work are not eligible for funding; the Fund generally does not provide solely completion funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application cost
rubrics_metrics.description: It is free to apply on or before the posted deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the deadline, applications may not be accepted or may require a late fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and budget currency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be written in English and accompanied by a budget translated into U.S. dollars; visual materials should be subtitled in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget size prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: The DFP prioritizes films with budgets under $1.2 million USD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a prioritization, not an absolute cutoff; consider how your budget aligns with this preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative and editorial control
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative and editorial control must be held by members of the films’ key creative teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, diversity, and perspective priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund seeks to uplift projects from filmmakers with distinct visions and meaningful connections to their work, elevating voices beyond borders and celebrating diverse filmmaking traditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is especially keen on stories reflecting pluralist society and diverse experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility regarding prior funding / fiscal sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior funding commitments or a fiscal sponsor are not required to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your written proposal should include a fundraising strategy outlining funds applied for versus funds secured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission / prior-applicant policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with the 2025 cycle, projects that have previously applied to the Documentary Fund are no longer eligible to reapply unless they have received an explicit written invitation to reapply from DFP staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces previous guidance, including language in past decline letters. Projects that previously received a grant are also not eligible to apply for additional funding through this open call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project length eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund supports feature-length documentaries (52 minutes and longer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hybrid/animated and experimental documentaries that meet length requirements are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund does not support fiction even if based on true events
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction films, even those based on true events, are not eligible; fiction filmmakers should consult the Sundance Institute Feature Film Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive budget requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every funding category requires a budget covering the costs of the entire project from development through distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a one- to two-page comprehensive line-item budget in U.S. dollars. A sample template is available but may be tailored; you may use your own format as long as it provides the costs of the entire project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising strategy required
rubrics_metrics.description: A fundraising strategy is required as part of the written proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define how you will raise your film budget (grants, broadcast licenses, private donations, in-kind support, crowdfunding, producer investment, fundraisers). Clearly distinguish between funds you have applied for and funds already secured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of impact (audience engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact/ audience engagement is a strategic campaign to encourage people and communities to move from passive to active participants on the issue the film addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement is distinct from distribution (getting films on screens) and from marketing/outreach (alerting viewers); it is designed to activate audiences and stakeholders toward a specific goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual sample minimums and competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Development applicants are encouraged (but not required) to include up to 15 minutes; production applications require minimum 10 minutes edited footage; post-production applications require minimum 20 minutes edited footage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production or post-production proposals with very short reels, trailers, teasers, or brief selects are not competitive against longer samples and may be moved to the development category. The Institute guarantees watching up to 30 minutes of visual material provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous work / director sample guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A visual sample that conveys the director’s creative perspective and ability to execute is preferred; for directorial debuts applicants may submit a film they have shot or edited or choose not to submit previous work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A previous work from a different member of the team (producer, editor, cinematographer) will not be considered. If you have multiple previous works or co-directors, select one previous work that best reflects the vision for your new project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted formats and delivery for visual material
rubrics_metrics.description: Only online streaming links are accepted; Vimeo or YouTube are recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide streaming link and password if applicable; film should be available for at least eight months after submission. Do not update or change your uploaded file or its password after submission. The Institute does not accept WeTransfer, Dropbox, Google Drive, or other file-transfer services. No DVDs accepted. Applicants in regions with significant internet impediments may email dfp@sundance.org to request an accommodation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application multistage review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals go through a multistage review, with selected submissions sent for Documentary Fund committee consideration; the committee meets to make funding recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately 2,000 proposals are reviewed annually and 25–30 films are funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria used by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated on several criteria, including strong artistic vision, compelling storytelling, conceptual excellence, contemporary cultural relevance, originality and creative risk-taking, feasibility, journalistic rigor (where applicable), and potential to reach and connect with an intended audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund spotlights new voices and artists bringing fresh perspectives, often through new creative frontiers. Film teams’ access to financial and creative resources and their connections to and engagement with the communities they work with are taken into consideration to prioritize funds for those who need them most.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Documentary Fund committee is composed of issue-area experts and professional film artists and curators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past panelists include curators, critics, filmmakers, editors, and producers (examples listed on the FAQ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: After submitting the online application, a confirmation page will appear and applicants should receive a confirmation email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no email is received, check spam filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to limited staff, Sundance cannot provide feedback to all applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that reach the final stage of review are eligible to receive feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for multiple submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may submit more than one proposal in the same round as long as they are for separate projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission updates policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may send significant updates to dfp@sundance.org, but the Documentary Film Program does not guarantee that updates will be incorporated into the project’s review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving other grants does not disqualify
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant receives a grant or award from another source, they are still eligible to apply for Sundance Institute funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant terms regarding rights and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are not recoupable and do not encumber exploitable rights; they are grants to the artist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To distribute funds, the Institute requires director and producer agreements and a clear chain of title. Grant agreements require logo acknowledgment in end credits and on promotional materials, submission of a high-resolution digital copy of the film, and narrative, financial, and distribution reports (and social impact reports if applicable). The Institute may request grantee participation in invitation-only creative community activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival submission and distribution independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving a Sundance Institute Documentary Fund grant does not guarantee screening at the Sundance Film Festival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees should submit completed work directly to the Sundance Film Festival; festival selection is independent of Fund awards. Likewise, projects not selected for Fund support remain eligible to apply to the Festival.

rubrics_metrics.name: No pre-application review of proposal elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute will not review elements of a proposal (deck, trailer, synopsis) before application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They only review complete proposals submitted through the online portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute does not accept phone inquiries about the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If questions remain after reading the FAQ, applicants may email dfp@sundance.org for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical support resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources are provided for reducing PDF file size and troubleshooting Vimeo uploads via linked help pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicants have region-specific internet access issues, they may request accommodations by email.
